questions.key_step: Common terms of two APs: first common term 11, difference lcm=12, count terms, sum
questions.justification: Short chain of routine A.P. facts, with one L.C.M. idea; numerical format.

questions.key_step: Equate A.P. sum of n angles to (n-2)180 and solve the quadratic
questions.justification: One standard formula and one quadratic; no decision beyond the setup.

questions.key_step: Non-trivial solution of a homogeneous system gives det = 0; expand using abc=45
questions.justification: A single familiar determinant condition and expansion; three or four steps.

questions.key_step: Roots of |A-xI|=0 are eigenvalues; trace of A^2 = (trA)^2 - 2|A|
questions.justification: One standard trace/determinant identity applied once.

questions.key_step: Pairs of terms equidistant from the ends have equal sums; count 203 pairs
questions.justification: One familiar A.P. property plus careful counting of the pairs.

questions.key_step: A adj(A^2) = A^-1 when |A|^2=1, so B = adj A and A(3B+I) = A-3I
questions.justification: Chain of adjoint/inverse identities with a sign trap; heavy identities but standard.

questions.key_step: S11=88 gives a+5d=8; roots T10,T11 give p and q by Vieta
questions.justification: Two familiar topics linked; several routine steps.

questions.key_step: Multiples of 6 not divisible by 4 or 9: remove multiples of 12 or 18, with 36 counted twice
questions.justification: Inclusion-exclusion with lcm; numerical answer and an ambiguous wording that causes slips.

questions.key_step: S_k = k(2k+1); the bracket collapses to 4n+5; solve the double inequality
questions.justification: Standard sums chained, then a simple integer inequality.

questions.key_step: Use the row sums and |A|=1 to find A, then compare A^-1 with alpha A + beta I
questions.justification: Routine algebra for a symmetric 2x2 matrix; several straightforward steps.

questions.key_step: A^2 = 3[[1,-1],[1,0]] and repeated squaring gives A^12 = 3^6 I
questions.justification: Repeated matrix multiplication with a periodic pattern; precision needed but no real insight.

questions.key_step: Coefficients sum to zero so x=1 is a root; equal roots force product 1
questions.justification: One neat observation followed by routine algebra.

questions.key_step: P_n = aP_{n-1}+bP_{n-2}; two instances give a,b; (u+v)^2=(u-v)^2+4uv
questions.justification: Hidden recurrence for power sums of roots plus a symmetric-function step; two ideas linked.

questions.key_step: ad=bc casework by number of distinct entries used
questions.justification: Careful casework with no options; one slip changes the count.

questions.key_step: alpha+beta=70; lambda coprime to 6 and smallest means alpha=5
questions.justification: Divisibility constraint plus minimisation by enumeration; modest chain.

questions.key_step: Hidden sum of squares gives GP; triangle inequalities give the interval
questions.justification: Hidden sum-of-squares identity linked with triangle inequalities and the golden-ratio interval.

questions.key_step: Rows sum to 3 so |det| <= 27 by Hadamard/eigenvalue bound
questions.justification: Answer is easy to guess but the bound needs a less familiar idea (Hadamard or eigenvalues).

questions.key_step: Solve three small linear systems for B1,B2,B3, then find |B| and trace
questions.justification: Three routine systems and a 3x3 determinant; long but straightforward.

questions.key_step: A orthogonal and A^2=A^T give A^3=I, so the expression collapses to 2A^3
questions.justification: One recognised idea (orthogonal matrix) then a short expansion.

questions.key_step: A=I+N with N^2=0 so A^k = I + kN; equation reduces to m^2+m=6
questions.justification: Needs the power pattern for the shear matrix and an inverse power; several stages.
